lesson.grammar_point: quantifiers: how much / how many / a lot of / a few / a little / not much / not many

vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: Things that people need every day, like food, soap and medicine
Comments about how good something is, and how to make it better
The tables, beds, chairs and sofas in a home
Good enough for the money, time or work that you give
To walk with a visitor and show them a place
You think something is very good, and you admire it
The rooms, buildings and equipment for a special use
An empty area that you can use

items.situation: How many people are in your team? Answer with a number and one more detail.
tips: There are... people in my team.

items.situation: How much time do you spend in meetings every week?
tips: I spend a lot of / not much time...

items.situation: Sarah asks: How many families stayed in the pilot? Answer.
tips: Eight families. A few of them...

items.situation: A director asks: How much money did you spend on furniture? Answer.
Give Sarah one piece of feedback about her program in Texas.
tips: I was impressed with... But maybe...

items.situation: Ask me two questions about my city: one with how many, one with how much.

listenings.text: Hi Fernando, it's Ricardo, from Finance. I have the numbers for the first two months of the pilot, and they are good. We hosted eight families, for a total of one hundred and ninety nights. We didn't spend much money on furniture, because a lot of it came from donations. We spent only four thousand reais. The supplies cost a little more than we assumed: about one thousand five hundred reais a month. So, how many apartments do we need next year? My answer is: maybe six. But I don't have much time this week, so let's talk about it on Monday.

Hi Fernando, it's Sarah. I'm at the airport now, and I just want to say thank you. I was really impressed with the pilot. In Texas, we have a lot of apartments, but we don't have many volunteers, and your volunteers make a big difference. I have a little feedback for you, too. The families need more space for the children, and a few of them asked for a washing machine in the apartment. The facilities are good, but I think a small playroom might be worth it. Let's put these ideas in our report next week. Bye for now!
